items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective), the agent implements a mostly sound FuXi-style three-stage U-Transformer cascade and proper verification pipeline on 5.625-degree ERA5 data, but its own trained cascade achieves metrics notably worse than the paper: skillful lead times (ACC >= 0.6) reach only 5.6 days for Z500 (vs. 10.5 days) and 2.4 days for T2M (vs. 14.5 days, with day-15 instability), while winning 0% of ACC and RMSE comparisons against the ECMWF ensemble mean (vs. 67.92% and 53.75%). Although the agent transparently supplements this by evaluating pre-computed published FuXi forecasts from WeatherBench2 (obtaining 11.35 days for Z500, 10.2 days for T2M, and 98%/96% ACC/RMSE win rates across 136 variable-lead cells), downloading the original authors' outputs does not substitute for reproducing the performance with the developed system, and the coarse-grid ERA5-truth evaluation also shifts the benchmark statistics relative to the paper's 240 combinations.

items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective), the agent implemented a valid three-stage U-Transformer cascade and plotted latitude-weighted ACC and RMSE across all eight target variables over 15 days, though using 2020 5.625° data and omitting GraphCast. While externally retrieved FuXi forecasts outperform HRES, the agent's own reduced-scale cascade performs notably worse than both HRES and the original paper (e.g., Z500 ACC crosses 0.6 near 5.3 days vs. ~10.5 days, and T2M diverges at extended leads).

items.content: Figure 2: Comparison of FuXi with ECMWF ensemble mean (EM) over 15-day forecasts. Top panels show normalized ACC difference and normalized RMSE difference between FuXi and ECMWF EM for Z500, T500, U50
items.reasoning: Evaluated under Mode A (Objective), the agent implements a valid three-stage U-Transformer cascade and plots normalized ACC and RMSE differences across the target variables, but its reduced-scale model performs substantially worse than the ECMWF ensemble mean at all leads (0% win rate vs. 67.92% ACC and 53.75% RMSE in the paper). Although the report also evaluates pre-computed WeatherBench2 FuXi forecasts, those external outputs do not represent the agent's trained system and fail to capture the day-9 transition where ECMWF EM overtakes FuXi.

items.reasoning: Using Objective Evaluation (Mode A), the agent implements a methodologically sound reduced-scale U-Transformer cascade on 5.625° ERA5 data and generates both Z500 forecast snapshots (days 1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 15) and spatial Z500 RMSE difference maps against HRES and ENS mean (days 5, 10). However, its trained model performs notably worse than HRES and ENS mean almost everywhere (day-10 Z500 snapshot RMSE of 97 m vs. 66 m for HRES, with predominantly negative skill differences) and damps anomalies on the coarse grid rather than preserving sharp synoptic trough-ridge patterns, though plotting regridded published FuXi forecasts alongside partially confirms lower RMSE than HRES. Additionally, compared to the target Figure 3, the spatial RMSE evaluation completely omits T2M maps and the 15-day lead time, and the spatial plots lack geographic projections, coastlines, and a Z500 colorbar.
